newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh oil barons criticised for hampering sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh oil barons criticised for hampering sell-off.

text.p: A senior Kazakh privatisation official has lashed out at Soviet-era oil barons for hampering the government's sale of the multi-billion dollar oil sector.
"I have said this before and repeat again: the oil sector must be privatised," Sarybai Kalmurzayev, chairman of the State Property Committee, told a news conference at the weekend.
"But there is a certain group of people who are afraid that they will lose everything if the oil-wells are torn from their control," he said.
Kalmurzayev was referring to the resource-rich country's powerful oil barons, some of whom oppose the government's planned rapid sell-off of troubled state-run companies.
He said oil enterprise chiefs had stirred up uncertainty among their workers, saying foreign investors could lead to job losses.
But Kalmurzayev said the situation in the potentially lucrative sector is unlikely to worsen further.
He singled out Mendesh Salikhov, head of the largest oil producer, Mangistaumunaigaz, as one of the main opponents of privatisation.
Mangistaumunaigaz, located in western Kazakhstan near the Caspian Sea, accounts for nearly one third of Kazakh oil output.
Kalmurzayev said workers there had not been paid for up to seven months. "If they really care so much about their workers, why haven't they paid them since last July?" he said.

Mangistaumunaigaz has been put up for tender, with 60 percent of shares available. Kalmurzayev said the sale of sizeable shareholdings to strategic investors was essential if the oil sector was to modernise and boost output.
"I do not say we should sell all shares in oil companies, but 50-60 percent of shares must be sold," he said.
Salikhov has said he wants to place shares on international markets, possibly in the form of depository receipts.
Kalmurzayev said the government aimed to sell up to 90 percent of shares in some oil enterprises.
Tuesday is the official deadline for bidders wishing to take part in a tender for 94.62 percent of shares in Karazhanbasmunaigaz, another oil company in western Kazakhstan.
The Karazhanbas oilfield has proven reserves of 226 million tonnes but Kalmurzayev said the enterprise's ageing Soviet technology meant the company could now only extract 85 million tonnes.
The government has so far managed to privatise only the Yuzhneftegaz oil company in central Kazakhstan.
It was sold to Canada's Hurricane Hydrocarbons Ltd for $120 million. The government hopes to earn over $2 billion in taxes and royalties over the next 20 years from the deal.

The privatisation process may accelerate after Kalmurzayev dealt the oil barons a blow last week when he dissolved Kazakhstanmunaigaz, the state holding company which controlled the Central Asian nation's oil and gas sector.

"Dissolving the holding... may be viewed as one of the forms of struggle around Kazakh oil companies... and a setback for the oil sector's structures wishing to hold on to their influence," the Panorama economic weekly said.

Most observers are sure the government will muster enough strength to overpower the oil chiefs and carry through the privatisation of Kazakhstan's oil sector, which sits on huge reserves worth billions of dollars.
